Ink, cream and red. Black squares, cream chain-mail, one red
The boldest. Two colours and cream: black bodies, a cream
line and one spot colour per fighter. It looks like a screen
print or a stencil, and it makes destruction and effects pop
The spot colour makes each fighter unmistakable at any zoom,
and the black-and-cream value split works on the sea, the
sky and at night. The cost is that everything must be
re-thought in two tones: skin, faces and wear all lose their
A palette-lookup shader: ink, paper and spot. Hard shadow
threshold, white-line outline pass, no ramp needed. The
cheapest fill of the four. The world must be limited to a
few colours too, or figures will not sit in it.
It commits the whole game to a restricted palette, including
biomes and effects, which is a large decision. Wounds and
blood lose their colour language (blood becomes the spot
colour or cream). Procedural planets need a two-tone
Common rules kept in every direction: the value rule (dark bodies, light gear), the two-tone edge, the far beacon, the violet Anti-hero lane, and no borrowed look. See docs/art/directions.md.
